facts.text: The authors computationally screened 38,326 Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions with each elemental concentration varied from 2.5 to 40 at.% in 2.5 at.% increments.
The screened composition selected for experimental study was Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 (at.%), chosen for minimum VEC together with a relatively high predicted Young’s modulus.
Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 was prepared by arc melting under argon.
The designed alloy was tested in the as-cast state by room-temperature compression at a quasi-static strain rate of 5 × 10^-4 s^-1.
The designed Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 alloy retained a single-phase BCC structure.
The reduced VEC was proposed to lower the Peierls–Nabarro barrier and promote shear instability, thereby increasing dislocation mobility and shear plasticity.
Abundant deformation slip lines were associated with delayed initiation of brittle cracks and continued work hardening.
Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 had much greater room-temperature compressive fracture strain than equimolar NbMoTaVW.
The compressive fracture strain was 35.7 ± 0.9%, compared with approximately 2% for equimolar NbMoTaVW.
The designed alloy had a slightly lower compressive yield strength than equimolar NbMoTaVW.
The designed alloy's compressive yield strength was 1115 ± 18 MPa, versus approximately 1246 MPa for equimolar NbMoTaVW.
Slip and work hardening enabled the designed alloy to reach a compressive strength of 2550 ± 75 MPa.
